_readme: A standardized draft-pick value curve, used as the Efficiency grade's
baseline instead of comparing picks against the actual outcomes of the
same class. Tommy's original point: the expected value of a given draft
slot should be roughly constant year to year — 1.01 should mean about
the same thing whether we're grading 2019's draft or 2025's. Deriving
the baseline from real players actually taken in each specific class
couldn't do that (a strong or weak class distorts its own curve), so
this file is a fixed, external reference instead: real KeepTradeCut
dynasty rookie-pick trade values (keeptradecut.com/trade-calculator),
1QB format (this league starts 1 QB, not Superflex).
Follow-up from Tommy: he doesn't have manual draft data before 2024
anyway, so a single fixed baseline for the past is fine — but asked for
genuine year-specific values where the real KTC futures market actually
supports it, i.e. for drafts going forward. That's what 'year' means
below: the values[year] each season's report card should use IS that
season's own year-specific curve when we have one, falling back to the
nearest year on file otherwise (see build.py/parse.pick_values_for_season).
values[year][round][i] = expected dynasty value of the (i+1)-th pick in
that round (0-indexed list, so values['2026']['1'][0] is 2026's pick
1.01). Only rounds 1-4 are populated — no manual_draft file on record
has ever gone past round 4 (checked 2024.csv/2025.csv), so there's
nothing to grade beyond that yet.
KTC assumes a 12-team league (12 picks per round); this league has 10.
No rescaling needed for that — pick 1.01 is 1.01 regardless of league
size, and our own worst pick in a round is real pick 10, which this
file already prices at its true position on the curve (index 9,
0-indexed) rather than being dragged toward an 11th/12th-pick average.
We simply never reference index 10/11 (KTC's picks 11/12).
HOW EACH YEAR WAS SOURCED, exactly, snapshotted 2026-08-15:
- values['2026']: KTC's trade calculator only ever carries full exact
per-pick prices (1.01, 1.02, ... 4.12) for the single imminent/current
draft class — confirmed directly (checked rawPlayers on the live
page; only 2026 had position='RDP' entries matching 'Pick R.PP',
2027/2028 did not). Read straight from the site's own in-page
dataset, not OCR'd or hand-typed off a screenshot.
- values['2027'] and values['2028']: KTC does NOT carry exact per-pick
prices for years beyond the imminent one — only three coarser
Early/Mid/Late tiers per round (also read directly from the site,
e.g. '2027 Early 1st' = 7345, 1QB). To keep the same fine-grained
12-pick-per-round shape instead of downgrading to 3 buckets, each
2026 pick was scaled by the ratio of its own tier's price in the
target year vs. 2026 (e.g. pick 1.02 sits in Round 1's 'Early' tier;
= 2026's real 1.02 (6544.32) x 1.1885). This preserves real pick-to-
pick shape while reflecting the real, live class-strength signal KTC
actually publishes for future years — a defensible approximation, not
independently-sourced exact data the way 2026's own row is.
- Every draft season this league actually has on file (2024, 2025) grades
against values['2026'] by nearest-year fallback, same as any future
season beyond 2028 would fall back to values['2028'] — see
parse.pick_values_for_season's clamp-to-nearest-year logic. Add a new
values['20XX'] entry here (repeat the tier-scaling approach above,
or a fresh exact snapshot if KTC has since made that year the
imminent one) whenever a future season's grading should stop using
the fallback.
source: keeptradecut.com/trade-calculator — '2026 Pick R.PP' exact prices; 2027/2028 scaled from 2026 by real Early/Mid/Late tier ratios (see _readme)
